title: Punjabi Singer Inder Kaur Found Dead in Canal — Canada-Based Ex-Boyfriend Accused of Kidnapping and Murder
excerpt: The 29-year-old artist was allegedly abducted at gunpoint after refusing a forced marriage proposal. Her accused killer fled to Canada via Nepal.
body:
The Punjabi music industry is in shock after singer Inder Kaur — known for hits like *Jija*, *Kisaan Anthem 2*, and *Akad* — was found dead in Ludhiana's Neelo Canal on May 19, nearly a week after she went missing. She was 29.

Her family has accused Sukhwinder Singh, a man from Moga district who holds Canadian permanent residency, of kidnapping her at gunpoint and murdering her after she refused his marriage proposal. According to police, Singh fled India through Nepal and is believed to have returned to Canada.

## A Friendship That Turned Fatal

Inder Kaur met Sukhwinder Singh on Instagram about three years ago, her family told police. What began as a casual friendship soured when she discovered he was already married with children. She ended contact. He allegedly refused to accept her decision.

On May 13, Kaur disappeared. Her family says Singh, along with his father Pritam Singh and an associate named Karamjit Singh, abducted her at gunpoint from Ludhiana. Police recovered a car near the canal in which she had allegedly been forced to travel.

Six days later, her body was pulled from the Neelo Canal and sent to Samrala Civil Hospital for postmortem.

## A Diaspora Connection That Complicates Justice

What makes this case especially troubling — and especially relevant to the NRI community — is the accused's cross-border escape. Sukhwinder Singh reportedly left India through Nepal, a common route for fugitives seeking to avoid airport surveillance. If he has indeed returned to Canada, Indian authorities will need to navigate extradition channels to bring him to justice.

For the Indian diaspora in Canada, cases like these are a painful reminder that geographic distance can be weaponised to evade accountability. Canada's Punjabi community, one of the largest outside India, has been vocal about honour-based violence and coercion — and Inder Kaur's death is likely to reignite those conversations.

## The Music Industry Mourns

Inder Kaur was a rising voice in the Punjabi music scene. Her energetic tracks and strong stage presence had built her a loyal fanbase. Her last Instagram post — a photo in a brown shirt, shared five days before her body was found — has turned into a makeshift memorial, with fans flooding the comments with tributes and questions about how it appeared while she was missing (some suspect it was a scheduled upload).

Fellow artists and industry figures have expressed outrage, with many calling for stronger protections for women in the entertainment industry.

## Where the Investigation Stands

Ludhiana police have arrested Karamjit Singh and are actively searching for Sukhwinder Singh and other associates. The case has been registered as a kidnapping and murder. Investigators are reportedly working with immigration authorities to trace Singh's movements out of the country.

Punjab Chief Minister's office has not yet issued a public statement, but pressure is mounting on social media for a swift resolution.

## What NRIs Should Know

This case sits at the intersection of celebrity culture, gender violence, and the complexities of transnational crime. For NRIs following from Canada, the UK, or the US, there are uncomfortable questions: How does the diaspora community respond when one of its own is accused of this kind of violence? What obligations do host countries have to cooperate on extradition?

Inder Kaur's music will live on streaming platforms worldwide. But her story is now about something far larger than music — it's about whether justice can cross borders as easily as her killer apparently did.
nri_angle: The accused, Sukhwinder Singh, holds Canadian permanent residency and allegedly fled India through Nepal to escape prosecution — raising urgent questions about NRI-linked honour crimes and cross-border fugitives.
